title: CMP (11,11,10) packed vertex attribute decoder oracle
purpose: Render an 8-cell grid where each cell is filled via the NV2A CMP attribute format (3 signed-normalized components packed into a 32-bit word: X bits 0-10 / 1023, Y bits 11-21 / 1023, Z bits 22-31 / 511). The DIFFUSE attribute is bound as TYPE_CMP with one packed word per vertex; the passthrough VS routes DIFFUSE -> COLOR; the framebuffer clamps to [0,1]. The 8 cells encode the ±1 corners of the unit cube so the decoded output lands at saturated 0/255 RGB cube colors. Catches bitfield-range/shift-offset errors (would misread neighboring component bits), sign-extension bugs (the BLACK cell at -1/-1/-1 would decode positively and saturate to non-BLACK), component-ordering bugs (RED <-> BLUE swap at asymmetric corners), and renderer-path divergences between GL's GLSL bitfieldExtract shader-side decode (vsh.c:203-208) and Metal's CPU-side decode (mtl/vertex.c:130-157). Does NOT catch sub-LSB divisor errors (1023 vs 1024 is ~0.25 LSB at byte quantization, invisible) or missing-decoder-side-clamp (framebuffer clamping subsumes it for negatives); intermediate-normal coverage with a custom (normal+1)*0.5 VS for that detection is filed as a second-wave follow-up. The 8-cell 4x2 grid produces seam pixels under retina downsample; compare_overrides relaxes max_changed_pct/min_signal_match_pct for grid pattern but tightens threshold=2 so saturated-corner reads are nearly byte-exact (catches 8-LSB+ scale errors at the corners).
